formation.explanation: Leader appends proposals with term and index and queues its own persistence-dependent acknowledgment. Follower verifies log prefix, appends a nonconflicting suffix and queues an acknowledgment. Leader consumes successful progress, asks tracker for committed candidate, and commits only a matching current-term entry. Commit updates propagate by append; committed entries are delivered through Ready with snapshot and local stability restrictions. Tracker aggregates only configured voters: majority takes the quorum-order statistic of Match; joint configuration takes the minimum of both majorities. Leader heartbeat commit is capped at recipient Match. Followers recover missing prefixes through probes or snapshots, and application remains separate from commit.

context.explanation: Campaign changes role and normally increments term; self-vote waits for persistence. Candidate polls responses of the matching election type and becomes leader on VoteWon. Higher-term messages normally step down; pre-vote has explicit exceptions. Reset clears progress and readOnly tracking; obsolete messages are filtered, with explicit snapshot completion handling for stale local append responses. Campaign admission checks voter eligibility, pending snapshot and unapplied committed configurations. Timer-driven quorum checks can step a leader down. Transfer attempts block proposals until target catch-up and TimeoutNow, authority loss, target removal or election-timeout abort. Startup restores term/vote/configuration and durable log while starting as follower.

connection.explanation: Term filtering, reset of progress and the current-term commit condition connect eligible support to authority. Durable log and committed snapshot state survive role transitions while transient vote and progress accounting resets. Configuration installation replaces aggregation context and can itself advance commitment. Ready separates delivery from storage and application completion. Configuration changes activate on application; joint decisions require both voter sets. Removing a voter preserves its progress while it remains in the outgoing set. Committed entries and application completions are term-independent, but volatile replication support and votes are reset. Old pre-commit read requests may be retried internally with fresh authority checks; already outstanding read quorum state is reset. Node dispatch serializes state mutation while permitting new messages and configuration application during a pending Ready.

grounding.derivation: ReadOnlySafe promises linearizable read safety; Node and RawNode ReadIndex describe a returned index as the fence after which prior read requests may safely be processed. In a single log history with a completed write before invocation, a certificate for an earlier prefix cannot suffice when the local application also excludes that write. The API permits lost requests, so the requirement is implication from emitted certificate, not guaranteed success. StepDownOnRemoval is optional and contains no disclaimer weakening ReadOnlySafe when false. The inspected interfaces impose no immediate shutdown or read-rejection duty on removal; Node itself blocks proposals but routes reads independently.
grounding.applicability: Actual removal was committed and applied before the surviving voter campaigns and applies a later write. No higher-term message is forged or suppressed: the new singleton has no reason to send to removed nodes. The old node is queried before periodic quorum loss changes its role, a legal ordering of asynchronous inputs.
alternatives: StepDownOnRemoval=true causes pending/no-certificate behavior in this history and is a valid protection.
Embedding applications may stop removed nodes, limiting exposure; that does not establish protection in the selected live-library scope.
A later CheckQuorum may step down, but future role correction cannot justify an earlier unsafe certificate.
